title: tenant-routing-controls-architectural-sketch
body:
Purpose

Notes and an early design sketch for tenant- and org-aware routing controls. This is a working doc: goal is to capture options, trade-offs, and concrete implementation sketches so infra + serving + product teams can iterate. Focus: mapping contractual tiers and operational quotas into runtime routing decisions, noisy-neighbor mitigation, and multi-region consistency for enforcement.

Short summary of the problem

We serve many customers (tenants) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. Requests must be routed to the appropriate serving pool with the following constraints:
- honor customer tiering (free/dev/standard/premium/enterprise) and per-contract SLAs for latency and availability
- enforce per-tenant quotas and unit economics controls (tokens, embeddings units, bandwidth)
- detect and mitigate noisy neighbors (bursting clients that harm others in a shared pool)
- support multi-region affinity and failover while keeping quota enforcement coherent
- minimize tail-call latency and avoid synchronous calls to a central control plane on the critical path where possible

Design principles

1) Decision locality: keep per-request routing decision data local and cached at edge/gateway. Central control plane manages policy authoring, distribution, and auditing.
2) Eventual correctness for non-critical enforcement: soft quota signals may be slightly stale in multi-region; hard enforcement uses local leases or tokens.
3) Graceful degradation: when policies are stale or control plane unreachable, fall back to safe defaults per contract.
4) Observability-first: every decision point emits structured events (policy id, revision, tenant id, reason) for debugging and billing.
5) Minimal cross-talk: use per-tenant queueing and shaping rather than global throttles where possible.

Entities and data model (simplified)

We store a tenant metadata record in the control plane. Excerpt of the conceptual table (not actual DB schema):

TENANT_RECORD sample rows (conceptual)
- tenant_id: t_1234
- org_id: org_88
- tier: enterprise|premium|standard|dev|free
- primary_region: us-west1
- allowed_regions: [us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1]
- quota_profile: q_78
- sla_profile: s_9
- noisy_neighbor_policy: {mode:shield|throttle|dedicated_fallback}
- dedicated_pool_id: dp_42 (nullable)

Policy objects (versioned)
- quota_profile: token_bucket parameters, burst allowance, refill schedule, cost-center mapping
- sla_profile: latency_percentiles targets per route, error budgets, retry budgets
- routing_policy: candidate_pools ordered by preference with cost/latency weights and preconditions (e.g., "if dedicated_pool present then route there unless pool_degraded_at > 5m")

Control plane responsibilities

- Author and store tenant records and policy objects (git-backed change history + approvals)
- Distribute policy snapshots to regional config caches (push + incremental patch topics)
- Provide realtime overrides and emergency kill switches
- Maintain usage ledger streams for billing and capacity signals
- Health/telemetry ingestion and anomaly detection (noisy neighbor detectors)

Runtime decision flow (high-level)

Client -> Edge Gateway -> Local Policy Cache -> Local Quota/Token Engine -> Pool Dispatcher -> Serving Pool

1) Edge Gateway extracts tenant_id from auth token (or request header for enterprise-private)
2) Edge checks local policy cache for tenant_record (cached snapshot with revision id). If cache miss, use fallback rules and request async refresh from control plane.
3) Evaluate routing_policy: compute prioritized candidate pools (dedicated, regional-hosted, spillover). Apply simple filters: region allowed, capacity flag, SLA compatibility.
4) Quota check: consult local token-engine; attempt to reserve X units. Token engine prefers local leases; if not available, allow controlled wait/queue and then reject or redirect to degraded path (e.g., lower-cost model or rate-limited mode)
5) Dispatch to chosen pool. Attach route metadata (policy_id, revision, decision_reason) to request for observability.

Quota enforcement options (trade-offs)

Option A: Centralized counters (strongly consistent)
- Pros: exact accounting, simple for billing and strict contract enforcement
- Cons: adds cross-region latency; single point of contention; not resilient to control-plane outages

Option B: Sharded/local token-bucket with periodic reconciliation (recommended default)
- Approach: control plane publishes quota_profiles to each region. Each region maintains local token buckets derived from tenant quota and a lease window (e.g., local allocation = floor(total_quota * region_weight)). Reconciler periodically (every 10s-60s) pulls usage deltas and adjusts allocations.
- Pros: low-latency checks, scalable, resilient
- Cons: allows small temporary overage across regions; needs reconciliation for billing accuracy

Option C: Hybrid hard enforcement for enterprise contracts + soft enforcement for others
- Enterprise customers get near-real-time central accounting endpoints (fast-path RPC to control plane with local caching fallback). Everyone else uses sharded token buckets.

Noisy neighbor detection & mitigation patterns

Detection signals (examples):
- tenant-contributed increase in per-pool queue length or scheduling delay
- sustained drop in other tenants' p95/p99 latencies in same pool after a tenant's surge
- rapid token consumption spikes beyond historical baseline + model usage pattern mismatch

Mitigation strategies (ordered by intrusiveness):
1) Local shaping: apply per-tenant rate limit at gateway, smoothing bursts with leaky-bucket.
2) Priority queuing: degrade lower-priority tenants in the same pool while preserving guaranteed latency for SLA tiers.
3) Cost-based reroute: redirect heavy workloads to cheaper/less-loaded model variants or quantized model variants (notify tenant).
4) Burst carve-outs and temporary dedicated lanes: assign temporary sub-capacity or small dedicated pool slices for a noisy tenant.
5) Forced dedicated fallback: for contractual customers we can move tenant to dedicated pool (if available); otherwise notify sales/ops for contract escalation.

Implementation sketch: local noisy neighbor module

- Runs in each region alongside the dispatcher and token engine.
- Ingests local metrics for pool-level latency, per-tenant usage, queue lengths.
- Applies anomaly detection (running z-score, short-window vs long-window baseline).
- Emits a tenant_action event when thresholds crossed: {tenant_id, window_ms, action: throttle|prioritize|route-change, reason, policy_id}
- Downstream components subscribe and apply action via the normal routing stack (idempotent).

Multi-region constraints and replication model

Key decisions:
- Config distribution (policies, quota profiles) is push-based with sequence numbers and compact deltas over a pub/sub topic replicated to regions.
- Usage ledger replication is append-only streaming to the control plane for authoritative billing. Local aggregators batch and compress events.
- For quotas we intentionally accept short-term divergence. Reconciliation model: use assignment windows (minute-level) where each region is given a provisional allocation; final allocation gets reconciled hourly for billing.

Failure modes and fallbacks

- Control plane unreachable: region continues with last-known policy snapshot; local token engine continues with local allocations; if allocation exhausted, apply safe fallback (route to lower-SLO pool or return 429).
- Regional partition: requests from partitioned region use local caches; cross-region failover respects 'allowed_regions' + read-only fallback.
- Quota overshoot discovered during reconciliation: generate billing adjustments and optionally throttle top offenders retroactively if contract allows.

APIs and contract-level knobs (sketch)

1) Policy authoring API (control plane admin):
- PUT /tenants/{id}/policy_snapshot (accepts versioned policies)
- GET /tenants/{id}/policy_snapshot?revision=

2) Runtime query API (for special flows):
- GET /runtime/tenants/{id}/routing-hints (fast read cache path)

3) Local runtime push endpoints (edge -> region):
- POST /region/{r}/reserve (tenant_id, units, correlation_id) -> success|deferred|rejected
- POST /region/{r}/release (for best-effort returned units)

4) Auditor/telemetry: event types: policy_eval, quota_reserve, throttle_action, route_decision, overflow_event

Operational considerations

- SLOs for policy propagation: aim for sub-5s for critical overrides, but regular policy updates can be eventual up to 1m.
- Capacity planning: compute per-tenant expected allocation across regions based on historical footprint and contractual allowed_regions. Use that for reserved pool sizing and burst budget.
- Testing: Chaos tests that simulate control-plane outage, regional partition, and noisy tenant surges. Verify that fallbacks are safe and that billing reconciliation works end-to-end.

Open questions / items for follow-up

- What strictness do we want for enterprise hard-enforcement vs developer self-serve? Define clear contract language for allowed temporary overages and reconciliation windows.
- How many allocation shards/regions to support per tenant before overhead grows? (1 vs N regional allocations)
- Should we expose tenant-facing backpressure signals (e.g., advisory headers) telling clients to retry with exponential backoff or to reduce batch sizes?
- Design the UI/console surfaces for customers to see current allocation, recent throttles, and overflow events.

Next steps (near term)

- Align on hybrid quota model: adopt Option B as default, Option C for enterprise. (owner: Priya)
- Prototype local token engine with lease-based regional allocations (POC in staging). (owner: Evan)
- Implement noisy-neighbor local detector + event schema; feed into existing pool-scaling pipelines. (owner: Diego)
- Draft SLA language for reconciliation windows for billing + template messages for customers on throttling. (owner: Ava)

Appendix: example policy DSL (informal)

policy tenant:t_1234 {
  tier: "premium"
  primary_region: "us-west1"
  routing: [
    {pool: "dedicated_dp_42", condition: "available && healthy"},
    {pool: "hosted_us_west", weight: 0.7},
    {pool: "hosted_spillover", weight: 0.3}
  ]
  quota {
    units_per_minute: 120000
    burst_tokens: 20000
    shard_weights: {us-west1:0.8, us-east1:0.2}
    enforcement: "local_lease"
  }
  noisy_neighbor_mitigation: "priority-queue"
}

(End of sketch)
